content_html:
Machu Picchu remains one of the most fascinating destinations in the world, and planning your trip in 2025 is key to enjoying it to the fullest. In this guide, we tell you everything you need to know about tickets, the best time to travel, transportation options and practical tips to make your experience unforgettable.

1. How to Buy Tickets for Machu Picchu in 2025?

Tickets to Machu Picchu sell out quickly, especially in high season (May to September). In 2025, the Peruvian government continues to regulate access to preserve the archaeological site, so it is advisable to purchase tickets with 3 to 6 months in advance.

Types of Tickets:

  • Machu Picchu Solo: Access to the Inca citadel.
  • Machu Picchu + Huayna Picchu: Includes the hike to the iconic Huayna Picchu mountain.
  • Machu Picchu + Machu Picchu Mountain: A more challenging climb but with panoramic views.
  • Machu Picchu + Inca Bridge: A less demanding option for those seeking history and nature.

Official purchase: www.machupicchu.gob.pe
You can also consult us GT Peru Travel to be able to make your purchase.

2. What is the Best Time to Visit Machu Picchu?

Dry Season (May – September):

  • Clear skies and spectacular views.
  • Greater influx of tourists, so it is recommended to book in advance.

Rainy Season (November – March):

  • Fewer tourists and impressive green landscapes.
  • Possibility of rain, so it is important to wear waterproof clothing.

If you want to avoid crowds and enjoy good weather, the months April and October They are ideal.

3. How to Get to Machu Picchu?

Option 1: Train from Cusco or Ollantaytambo

  • Companies: PeruRail and IncaRail.
  • Route: Cusco/Ollantaytambo Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Pueblo).
  • Duration: 1.5 to 4 hours depending on the starting point.

Option 2: Inca Trail (4 days / 2 days)

  • The favorite option for trekking lovers.
  • Reservations more than 6 months in advance are required.

Option 3: Alternative Route through Hydroelectric

  • More economical and with adventure.
  • It requires a 2 to 3 hour walk from Hidroeléctrica to Aguas Calientes.

4. Practical Tips for your Visit

  • Bring your passport: It is mandatory to enter.
  • Layered clothing: Due to climatic variations, wear light clothing and a waterproof jacket.
  • Sunscreen and repellent: Essential to protect you from the sun and insects.
  • Respect the rules: Machu Picchu is a World Heritage Site, so follow the rules for its conservation.

Ready to experience the magic of Machu Picchu in 2025?

Organize your trip in advance and get ready to discover one of the most amazing places on the planet.
